verdict.rationale: PostHog AI, built into the product, accepts plain-English requests. It queries data, writes SQL, builds insights, and also takes actions such as creating dashboards, surveys, alerts and feature flags. The same natural-language control is available from Slack (@PostHog) and from any MCP client via plain-text prompts. One hands-on community report says the in-app assistant could not create a SQL-based cohort and slowed the UI badly after a couple of prompts. That limits breadth and polish, but it does not contradict the core capability. Missing for 10: independent corroboration that natural-language operation works reliably across product areas, and evidence addressing the reported cohort-creation gap and UI performance problem.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Ask it a question in plain English and it queries your data, builds the insight, writes the SQL, or finds the session replay – then explains what it found.
PostHog AI creates dashboards, surveys, alerts, and feature flags, edits filters in the UI alongside you, and remembers what it learns about your product between conversations.
Mention the bot with a question about your product data and it answers in-thread using the PostHog MCP.
with just plain text questions your agents can ship a feature flag from a prompt, dig into a stack trace without leaving your editor, run a HogQL query through Claude
